title.orig: A Letter of Mr. Isaac Newton … containing his New Theory about Light and Colors
title.en: A New Theory about Light and Colours
title.zh: 关于光和颜色的新理论

year_display.zh: 1672 年（自剑桥寄出，落款 1671/2 年 2 月 6 日）

edition.en: Newton’s letter to Henry Oldenburg as printed in the Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society, vol. 6, no. 80 (19 February 1671/2), pp. 3075–3087. The text was taken from Wikisource’s transcription and corrected against a scan of the original printing: about twenty errors of the transcription are put right, and Newton’s spellings (applyed, suspition, Prisme, more then) are kept. As in 1672, the numbered propositions skip from 3 to 5. An obvious misprint of 1672, “vary” for “very”, is corrected; the printer’s italics are not reproduced, nor are the two diagrams Newton refers to.
edition.zh: 牛顿致亨利·奥尔登堡的信，刊于《皇家学会哲学汇刊》第 6 卷第 80 期（1671/2 年 2 月 19 日），第 3075–3087 页。文本取自维基文库的录文，并对照原刊扫描本校正：改正了录文约二十处错误，保留牛顿的拼写（applyed、suspition、Prisme、more then）。命题编号像 1672 年原刊一样，从 3 直接跳到 5。原刊一处明显的误印（“vary”作“very”）已改正；排印时的斜体不再保留，牛顿提到的两幅图也不收。

basis.en: Published in 1672; Isaac Newton died in 1727.
basis.zh: 1672 年发表；牛顿卒于 1727 年。

note.en: Newton’s first published scientific paper, a letter to the Royal Society written when he was twenty-nine. Step by step, in a darkened room with a hole in the shutter, he shows that white light is a mixture of rays that bend by different amounts and carry different colours, and that no prism can change a colour once it has been separated. He also explains why he stopped grinding lenses and built a telescope with a mirror instead. It ends by inviting others to repeat the experiments and to tell him if he is wrong.
note.zh: 这是牛顿发表的第一篇科学论文，是他二十九岁时写给皇家学会的一封信。在一间窗板上开了孔的暗室里，他一步一步地证明：白光是由折射程度不同、颜色也不同的光线混合而成的，一种颜色一旦被分离出来，任何棱镜都不能再改变它。他还说明了自己为什么不再磨制透镜，转而造了一架用镜子的望远镜。信的结尾，邀请别人重复这些实验，如果他错了就告诉他。

excerpt.orig: And I shall not mingle conjectures with certainties.
excerpt.en: And I shall not mingle conjectures with certainties.
excerpt.zh: 我不想把猜测同确定的东西混在一起。

gloss.at: To perform my late promise to you
gloss.en: The letter is addressed to Henry Oldenburg, secretary of the Royal Society, who printed it in the Philosophical Transactions.
gloss.zh: 这封信写给皇家学会秘书亨利·奥尔登堡，由他刊登在《哲学汇刊》上。

gloss.en: Newton was then twenty-three. The dates are his own recollection, written down six years later.
gloss.zh: 那时牛顿二十三岁。这些日期是他六年之后凭记忆写下的。

gloss.at: Optick glasses of other figures than Spherical
gloss.en: Lenses ground to non-spherical curves, such as those Descartes recommended, were expected to cure the blurring of telescopes.
gloss.zh: 磨成非球面曲线的透镜，比如笛卡尔所推荐的那种，当时人们期望用它来消除望远镜的模糊。

gloss.at: the ratio of the sines, 20 to 31
gloss.en: The law of refraction: the sine of the angle of incidence bears a fixed ratio to the sine of the angle of refraction. A ratio of 20 to 31 is a refractive index of 1.55.
gloss.zh: 折射定律：入射角的正弦与折射角的正弦成固定的比例。20 比 31 相当于折射率 1.55。

gloss.en: Crossing, in the shape of an X.
gloss.zh: 交叉，像字母 X 那样。

gloss.en: The thin, invisible medium that many natural philosophers believed filled all space.
gloss.zh: 以太，当时许多自然哲学家认为充满整个空间的一种稀薄而看不见的媒质。

gloss.en: “Crucial experiment”, after Francis Bacon’s “instance of the fingerpost” (crux), the signpost at a crossroads: an experiment that decides between rival explanations. Hooke had used the phrase in Micrographia.
gloss.zh: 拉丁文，“判决性实验”，源于弗朗西斯·培根所说的“路标的事例”（crux，岔路口的指路标）：在相互竞争的解释之间作出裁决的实验。胡克在《显微图谱》里已经用过这个说法。

gloss.en: The Great Plague closed the University of Cambridge in 1665 and 1666, and Newton worked at his family’s farm in Lincolnshire.
gloss.zh: 大瘟疫使剑桥大学在 1665 和 1666 年关闭，牛顿回到林肯郡家里的农庄工作。

gloss.en: The four large moons of Jupiter, discovered by Galileo in 1610; his account of them is on this shelf.
gloss.zh: 木星的四颗大卫星，伽利略在 1610 年发现；他关于它们的记述也在这一架上。

gloss.at: like that I sent to London
gloss.en: Newton’s small reflecting telescope, about six inches long, shown to the Royal Society at the end of 1671. It led to his election as a Fellow, and to this letter.
gloss.zh: 牛顿那架约六英寸长的小型反射望远镜，1671 年底送到皇家学会展示。他因此当选为会员，也因此写了这封信。

gloss.en: The 1672 printing has no proposition numbered 4; this paragraph stands in its place.
gloss.zh: 1672 年原刊没有编号为 4 的命题；这一段就处在它的位置上。

gloss.en: “Kidney wood”, a Mexican wood whose infusion looks blue by reflected light and yellow by transmitted light; the effect is now known as fluorescence.
gloss.zh: 肾木，一种墨西哥木材，它的浸液在反射光下呈蓝色，在透射光下呈黄色；这种现象今天叫作荧光。

gloss.at: Mr. Hook somewhere in his Micrography
gloss.en: Robert Hooke’s Micrographia (1665), whose preface is on this shelf. Hooke, the Royal Society’s curator of experiments, became the sharpest critic of this paper.
gloss.zh: 罗伯特·胡克的《显微图谱》（1665），它的序言也在这一架上。胡克是皇家学会的实验主管，后来成了这篇论文最尖锐的批评者。

gloss.en: Minium is red lead; Bise, or blue bice, is a blue pigment made from copper.
gloss.zh: minium 是铅丹；bise（blue bice）即石青，一种用铜矿物制成的蓝色颜料。

gloss.en: Newton leans toward light as a stream of particles but keeps a “perhaps”. His next sentence, refusing to mix conjecture with certainty, became a rule for how he wrote.
gloss.zh: 牛顿倾向于认为光是一股粒子流，但保留了一个“也许”。他接下来那句不肯把猜测和确定混在一起的话，成了他写作的一条规矩。

gloss.en: The Royal Society of London, founded in 1660 to advance knowledge by experiment.
gloss.zh: 伦敦皇家学会，1660 年成立，宗旨是通过实验增进知识。

note.en: Newton’s first paper and a model of experimental argument: a hole in a shutter, two prisms, and white light shown to be a mixture of colours.
note.zh: 牛顿的第一篇论文，实验论证的典范：窗板上一个孔、两块棱镜，证明白光是多种色光的混合。
